tiers.smb: Under ~250 employees, or annual marketing budget under ~$1M (small/boutique agencies included)
tiers.mid_market: ~250–2,500 employees, active brand and media investment
tiers.enterprise: 2,500+ employees, or $1B+ revenue, or global / multi-brand footprint

routes.self_serve: Trial CTA dominates the routing screen; attributed signup on the product's site; activation tracked
routes.demo: Sales-led demo booked with the owning product team, pre-briefed with the snapshot
routes.consultative: One Stagwell conversation, multi-product capable, flagged first-class in CRM

overrides_in_order.why: multi-product opportunity outranks any single cell, whatever the tier
senior decision-makers get the portfolio conversation, not a single-product demo

notes: Attribution is always captured; contact rides with the route wherever it was given — a visitor who declines email keeps the on-screen snapshot and is logged anonymously. · follow_up retired Sep 2 at the client’s request (“we want everyone to end on book a demo, start a free trial or talk to Stagwell”): q5 lost its “Just exploring” chip with it, and the six SMB cells that nurtured now book a demo — the one ask every product can honestly make.
